answersTestFailures.failure: Acceptance 3 holds for this release and breaks across two: a legion binary of the previous release sends no keep field, is answered 202, reads that as neither success nor ErrNoHolder, and keeps its outbox row while Envoy also keeps the message, so the role's next holder gets the notice twice.
answersTestFailures.fix: INFRA-514's architect decided on 2026-10-31 that the answer is the release order, not a listener change: the legion binary carrying keep:false deploys before the Envoy listener carrying the kept lane. No listener code changed. The order is recorded in the three places the architect named: the pull request body's Not proven / risk, the envoy changelog fragment (packages/envoy/.changes/unreleased/pr2588-kept-role-lane.yaml, a RELEASE ORDER paragraph), and a comment at the keep:false send in packages/daemon/internal/notify/notify.go, which cites the tester's live measurement.
answersTestFailures.evidence: The duplicate is a duplicate and not a loss, which is why an order is enough: the tester measured the old publisher getting 'listener returned 202 Accepted' with errors.Is(err, ErrNoHolder) false and the kept lane then holding that message. Nothing in this repository can pin the order, since the Envoy listener and the legion binary are separate releases (.github/workflows/release-envoy-listener.yaml, release.yaml), and a test that read a workflow file would be the check-of-a-check the deployment instructions forbid.

forwardMerge.why: This round adds the release-order record beside the merge, so the diff is not the same diff and the head needs a full test round rather than the bare gates. The fingerprint's from is this branch's own base merge on each side (ddc0078d1e12 before, b1993dc02e14 after) rather than fork_point(base@origin | head): this branch brings its base in by merge, so that revset resolves to two revisions and jj refuses it. Posted as a comment on the pull request.
forwardMerge.rebuilt: Built the branch and ran its proof again at the merge head, as the reference requires after any forward merge.

trickyParts: The reference's fingerprint revset, fork_point(base@origin | head), does not resolve for this branch: it brings its base in by merge, so jj answers two revisions and refuses the diff. The fingerprint is taken from this branch's own base merge on each side instead, which is the same question (this change's own lines) asked of comparable trees, and the departure is stated in the pull request comment.
deviations: Acceptance 3's cross-release window is answered by a recorded release order rather than by code. INFRA-514's architect decided it on 2026-10-31 over a listener-side change, since the failure mode is a duplicate notice rather than a lost one, and the two artefacts are separate releases.
The forward-merge fingerprint is 'changed', not 'unchanged', so this head is not a confirmation: the full proof and every suite were re-run at it rather than the bare gates.
discoveredComplexity: The tester's first failure was a branch state rather than a defect, and no red test could pin it: GitHub runs no lane at all on a conflicting head, so a round can look untested when it is in fact unrunnable. The forward merge is what makes CI exist for this change; the first CI read of this pull request is the one that follows this push.
